title: 2009 AMC 12B Problem 10
statement: A particular \(12\)-hour digital clock displays the hour and minute of a day. Unfortunately, whenever it is supposed to display a \(1,\) it mistakenly displays a \(9.\) For example, when it is \(1{:}16\) pm the clock incorrectly shows \(9{:}96\) pm. What fraction of the day will the clock show the correct time?

solutions.text:
The hours containing a \(1\) are \(1, 10, 11, 12,\) so \(8\) of the \(12\) hours display correctly, a fraction \(\dfrac{2}{3}.\)

A minute is wrong if either digit is \(1\): the tens digit gives \(10\text{-}19\) (\(10\) minutes), and the ones digit adds \(01, 21, 31, 41, 51\) (\(5\) more), \(15\) in all. So \(\dfrac{45}{60} = \dfrac{3}{4}\) of minutes are correct.

The fraction of the day is \(\dfrac{2}{3} \cdot \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The hour is shown correctly unless it contains a \(1,\) namely hours \(1, 10, 11, 12\)
A minute is correct only when neither of its digits is a \(1\); count the bad minutes out of \(60\)
